html:
A Korean religious movement founded in 1860 by Choe Je-u. Its name means "Eastern Learning", set against the "Western Learning" of Catholicism. It mixed Confucian, Buddhist, Daoist and folk beliefs around the worship of Heaven.

It taught that Heaven dwells in every person, so all people are equal. That message spread fast among peasants crushed by taxes and corrupt officials in late Joseon. The government saw it as dangerous and executed Choe in 1864, but the movement went on in secret.

In 1894 Donghak followers led a great peasant revolt in the southwest under Jeon Bong-jun. The Joseon court asked Qing China for troops, Japan sent its own, and the clash between them became the First Sino-Japanese War. Japanese and government troops crushed the rebels, and the Gabo Reform followed.

In 1905 the movement renamed itself Cheondogyo, the Religion of the Heavenly Way. Its leader Son Byong-hi was one of the organisers of the March 1st Movement of 1919.
